text:
maya: Heads-up — we need to lock down span naming + attr set for LLM requests before the retention/ingest changes land. cc @sam @ravi

sam: +1. main goals: low-cardinality span names, clear semantics for tokens/cache/routing, and avoid exporting PII.

ravi: Agreed. I think span.name should be operation-level, not model-specific. e.g. `llm.generate`, `llm.embeddings`, `llm.rerank` so backends can aggregate.

leah: That helps aggregation, but we still need model identifier as an attribute for perf dashboards. Propose `model.family` and `model.variant`. family=gemini/llama, variant=13b-quant or similar. keep both limited vocab.

maya: +1 on model.family/model.variant. important: do NOT put full absolute path or commit hash in attributes (high cardinality). if we need exact version, route to trace logs only.

jordan: For token counts: llm.request_tokens, llm.response_tokens as ints. Also llm.input_length_chars maybe for correlating latency.

sam: Cache hits: we debated boolean vs enum. proposal: `kvcache.hit = true/false` and `kvcache.prefix_matched = true/false` for prefix cache separately. keep names short and stable.

ravi: Routing policy attrs: `routing.policy = latency|cost|region` and `routing.fallback = model.variant` when fallback happened. But fallback model.variant must be restricted to known set to avoid cardinality explosion.

leah: About exporters & retention: plan is to send full span to long-term storage only for sampled traces. But metrics derived from span attrs should be exported always (counts/histograms).

maya: Policy note: sampling rate should consider request token length (sample more for long requests) and errors. e.g. sample_rate = min(1, base * (1 + request_tokens/1000)) and force-sample on status!=OK.

jordan: Also need a short attribute map example for infra docs. here's a compact example we can copy into the console UI docs:

```
span.name = "llm.generate"
attributes = {
  "service.name": "redwood-inference",
  "model.family": "llama",
  "model.variant": "llama-2-13b-q4",
  "llm.request_tokens": 42,
  "llm.response_tokens": 128,
  "kvcache.hit": false,
  "kvcache.prefix_matched": true,
  "routing.policy": "latency",
  "routing.fallback": "ldraft-13b",
  "quota.bucket": "free-tier",
  "quota.exceeded": false
}
```

sam: That looks good. A couple more rules to encode in the spec:
- All attribute keys lowercase with dots.
- No free-text prompts in attrs. If teams need prompt fingerprints, store hashed_prompt_id only.
- Limit model.variant to a canonical registry name (we'll enforce in compile step).

leah: For backend exporters, we'll map `quota.bucket` -> metrics tag and keep retention shorter for free-tier buckets. Also need an opt-out flag for customer-requested export retention in private deployments.

ravi: One more security item: strip any user-provided metadata that could contain PII before creating span attrs. Ops-bot, can we add a lint that fails builds if new span attrs match suspicious keys (ssn, email, phone)?

ops-bot: deploy-checker: new span attribute linting rule added to infra-ci (rule span-attr-pii-blocklist). It will run on PRs to telemetry. :robot_face:

maya: Nice. Next steps: I'll draft a short RFC with the final list and examples, and a JSON schema for allowed model.variant values. Sam, can you own the console/table mapping for dashboards?

sam: Yep, I'll add mapping docs and a dashboard template. target: include in next week's release notes. :thumbsup:

jordan: Can we also add an example for function-calling traces? maybe `llm.call.function` span.name and `llm.function.name` attribute.

maya: Good catch — include function span names and set a rule: `llm.function.name` is sanitized and hashed if user-provided.

leah: I'll update retention matrix to use sampling heuristics + quota tags.

maya: Thanks everyone — I'll post the RFC link here when ready.
